title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a city during a major public event that created traffic conditions outside their normal operating range. Multiple vehicles became stranded when battery depletion forced them to stop in heavy congestion, requiring manual towing to remove them. At least one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks debris on the street.

The system was not designed or tested for the combination of extreme congestion, road closures, and hazardous road conditions that emerged during Fourth of July celebrations. A human dispatcher or operational limits system could have prevented deployment into the event area or withdrawn vehicles before battery levels became critical. The incident shows a gap between the traffic patterns the system was built to handle and the traffic patterns that actually occurred.

It is not established whether Waymo had specific policies against operating during major events, whether traffic predictions were available before deployment, or what battery reserves the vehicles maintained for contingencies.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations on Saturday after their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, predominantly Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display at the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. At least one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, though no injuries were reported.

Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to remove the stranded vehicles with tow trucks. One witness reported spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic as vehicles were cleared. The company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during major traffic disruptions. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to meet with stakeholders, including Waymo and other public and private partners, to discuss the incident and work toward smoother experiences for future events involving large crowds.
